newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan FIC up sharply at mid-session.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan FIC up sharply at mid-session.

text.p: Taiwan's First International Computer rose sharply at mid-session on Friday on news that it was negotiating an order with U.S.-based Compaq Computer Corp to make Compaq motherboards, brokers said.
After 65 minutes, First International was up T$0.90 to T$39.20 in the day's heaviest single trade volume of 13.58 million shares.
First International spokeswoman Wu Li-yin confirmed market rumours of the possible deal, but declined to say if the Compaq order was final.
"I can confirm that we are talking with Compaq, but we are also talking simultaneously with other companies, because we are primarily an OEM (original equipment manufacturing) firm," Wu said.
Brokers said investors were optimistic about the company's outlook.
"First International already enjoyed good fundamentals, and the deal gave investors even more enthusiasm," said Joe Chiou of Taiwan Securities Investment.
First International is Taiwan's second largest computer firm. -- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
